corpus.title: Manhunt after shooting at Swiss rave kills woman, 22, and injures five
corpus.signal_text:
Manhunt after shooting at Swiss rave kills woman, 22, and injures five
- Published
A manhunt is under way after a 22-year-old woman was killed and five others injured in a shooting at a rave in Switzerland.
The woman died at the scene in Aarau, police said. Those injured were four men and a woman aged between 24 and 27, all of whom are in hospital with injuries "ranging from minor to severe".
Organisers and performers said the shooting happened at a techno rave being held at a horse racing track in the town, which is located some 46km (29 miles) west of Zurich.
A police spokesperson told Swiss media on Sunday afternoon that they had "no concrete leads", having earlier said the shooter's identity and motives were unclear.
It is unlikely that they are still in Aarau, spokesman Bernhard Graser told Swiss newspaper Blick, but there is "no imminent danger".
The force said it had received an initial report of shots fired at the Schachen race track at 02:30 local time (01:30 BST).
A DJ who was due to perform until the scheduled end of the event at 02:00 said the incident occurred "straight after our set", in a post on social media.
Another performer, DJ Tekibo, said he had lost a friend in the incident. He wrote on Instagram that he was "still trying to process what happened".
Olivier Grein, whose firm Agency Events AG organised the event, said the company was "shaken" and would do all it could to support police.
An eyewitness told Blick that he "suddenly heard the gunshots" minutes after the music stopped at 02:30, initially believing they were fireworks.
He said he was told to hide by a man and a woman, the latter of whom was then shot.
Organisers had expected up to 3,500 people to attend. Police asked witnesses to submit photographs and video from the scene.
An area around the racing track, the town's swimming pool and sports field has been cordoned off, with the public urged to stay away.
A large contingent of officers has also been deployed beyond Aarau "as a precaution", Aargau Cantonal Police said.
An AFP journalist reported seeing armed officers deployed on the highway up to 30km (18 miles) from the site of the shooting.
Aarau, home to approximately 23,000 people, is less than 40km (25 miles) from the border with Germany, where local media reported police were supporting Swiss forces.

corpus.title: Switzerland rave shooting kills 1, injures 5 as police hunt those responsible
corpus.signal_text:
A 22-year-old woman was killed and five other people were wounded in a shooting early Sunday at a rave in northern Switzerland, authorities said, as police launched a large-scale search for those responsible.
The shooting happened in the Schachen area of Aarau, the capital of Switzerland’s Aargau canton, where the "Aarau Rave VOL. 7" was being held at a horse-racing track, according to Swiss broadcaster SRF.
Aargau cantonal police said the woman died from her injuries at the scene. Four men and another woman, all between the ages of 24 and 27, were taken to hospitals with injuries ranging from minor to serious.
All six victims are residents of Switzerland, police said.
Police spokesman Pascal Wenzel told SRF that authorities were alerted to the shooting shortly after 2:30 a.m. The event had been scheduled to end at 2 a.m., according to SRF, which cited information from the organizers’ website.
Authorities said the perpetrator or perpetrators remained unidentified and that possible motives and the circumstances surrounding the shooting were still unclear.
A large area surrounding the horse-racing track, swimming pool and nearby sports field was cordoned off as police searched the area. Authorities also increased their presence elsewhere in Aarau as a precaution and urged members of the public to stay away.
ALL 12 VICTIMS STABLE AFTER SHOOTING NEAR FESTIVAL AS TOLEDO POLICE PURSUE MULTIPLE LEADS
The response included police officers, firefighters and several emergency medical services, according to SRF. The broadcaster reported that a cantonal disaster-response unit, the Argus police special unit and a Swiss military Super Puma helicopter were also involved.
Police in neighboring Germany were also assisting with the search as part of routine cross-border cooperation, a spokesman in Freiburg told the German news agency dpa, according to SRF.
Police appealed to witnesses to provide investigators with videos or photographs from the event and established an information line for relatives and eyewitnesses.
Swiss DJ Tekibo, who performed at the rave, later wrote on Instagram that what happened was "absolutely heartbreaking" and said raves should be places of freedom and safety. He also said he had lost an "important friend," though SRF reported that it was not clear whom he was referring to.

The Associated Press contributed to this report.
